entry: Coalition of [[Nazi Germany]], the [[Kingdom of Italy]] and the [[Empire of Japan]] that fought the Allies in [[World War II]]. Its leading members shared far-right positions and opposition to the Allies, but coordination among them was minimal. The alliance grew from diplomatic efforts in the mid-1930s; the Tripartite Pact of 1940 formally integrated the military aims of Germany, Italy and Japan. At its zenith in 1942 the Axis held large parts of Europe, North Africa and East Asia through occupation, annexation or puppet states. Its defeat in 1945 ended it.

Central shaft for a rotating [[Wheel|wheel]] or [[Gear|gear]]. On wheeled vehicles the axle may be fixed to the wheels and turn with them, or stay fixed to the vehicle while the wheels rotate around it. In the latter case [[Bearing (mechanical)|bearings]] or bushings sit in a central hole in the wheel, and on bicycles such an axle is often called a spindle. A straight axle is a single rigid shaft connecting wheels on opposite sides of a vehicle. It keeps the wheels steady under heavy stress, which is why it is used on trains, the rear axles of commercial trucks and heavy-duty off-road vehicles. In many independent suspensions the axle shafts only transmit [[Torque|driving torque]] to the wheels. The [[Wheel and axle]] is one of the six classical simple machines, providing mechanical advantage by applying force to the larger wheel radius to produce greater torque at the smaller axle. The system emerged around 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia.

Salamander species native to the highlands of Mexico. Adults reach sexual maturity without metamorphosis and remain aquatic with external gills. Its natural habitat of lakes in the Valley of Mexico has largely been destroyed, first by drainage initiated by the [[Aztecs]] and accelerated in the 20th century, and by introduced [[Tilapia|tilapia]] and [[Carp|carp]]. The species is listed as critically endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, with around 50 to 1,000 adult individuals left in the wild. A large captive population is used extensively in research, because axolotls can regenerate limbs, gills, and parts of their eyes and brains. The species is also a [[Model organism]].

South American psychoactive decoction prepared from *Banisteriopsis caapi* vine and a DMT-containing plant. Indigenous peoples of the Amazon and Orinoco basins have used it in traditional medicine and [[Shamanism|shamanism]]. The word comes from [[Quechuan languages]] and means spirit rope. Its use spread to [[Brazil]], where syncretic religions made it widespread by the mid-20th century, and later to Europe and North America. Its effects come mainly from DMT, which harmala alkaloids make orally active by inhibiting monoamine oxidase. Higher doses of ayahuasca or harmala alkaloids may increase risks. DMT is internationally controlled, but the plants containing it are not regulated under international law.

Long-fingered [[Lemur|lemur]] native to [[Madagascar]]. It is the world's largest nocturnal primate and the only living member of the genus *Daubentonia*. It practices percussive foraging: it taps on trees, listens for echoes from grub-filled hollows, gnaws a hole with its forward-slanting incisors and extracts the larvae with its thin middle finger. This method takes up 5–41% of its foraging time. Only the striped possum and trioks, marsupials of northern Australia and New Guinea, are known to forage this way. The aye-aye is classified as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. A second species, *Daubentonia robusta*, appears to have become extinct within the last 1,000 years.

Russian-born American novelist and philosopher. Born in [[Saint Petersburg]], she emigrated to the United States in 1926. Her novels include *The Fountainhead* (1943) and *Atlas Shrugged* (1957), and she developed a philosophical system she named Objectivism. She advocated [[Reason|reason]], rejected faith and religion, and supported rational egoism and [[Laissez-faire|laissez-faire capitalism]]. Rand condemned the initiation of force and opposed [[Libertarianism|libertarianism]], though she is often associated with the modern libertarian movement in the United States. Her books have sold over 37 million copies. Academic philosophers have generally ignored or rejected her philosophy, with critics arguing that her approach is polemical and her work lacks methodological rigor.

City on the Saryu River in [[Uttar Pradesh]], India. It is the administrative headquarters of Ayodhya district. Hindus regard it as the birthplace of [[Rama]] and the first of seven most important pilgrimage sites. Jain texts describe it as the birthplace of five tirthankaras, and early Buddhist and Jain texts record visits by Gautama Buddha and Mahavira. Historically known as Saketa, it was renamed Ayodhya during the Gupta period. In 1992 a Hindu mob demolished the Babri mosque, built in 1528–29 under [[Babur]]. In 2019 the Supreme Court of India ordered the land handed to a trust to build the Ram Mandir, which was consecrated in January 2024.

Brazilian racing driver and philanthropist. He competed in [[Formula One]] from 1984 to 1994, winning three world championships with [[McLaren]] in 1988, 1990 and 1991, and 41 Grands Prix. His rivalry with Alain Prost produced title-deciding collisions at Suzuka in 1989 and 1990. He was known for his wet-weather performances. He was killed in a crash while leading the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix at Imola, driving for Williams. He was the last fatality in Formula One until Jules Bianchi in 2014, and his accident influenced later car safety improvements. He founded the Instituto Ayrton Senna, which as of 2023 had impacted over 36 million Brazilian students.

[[Alternative medicine]] system with historical roots in the [[Indian subcontinent]]. Ayurveda is heavily practiced in India and Nepal, where as much as 80% of the population report using it. Its name comes from [[Sanskrit]] and means knowledge of longevity. Therapies include herbal medicines, special diets, [[Meditation|meditation]], [[Yoga|yoga]], massage, laxatives, enemas and medical oils. Classical texts, dating in their present form to the first centuries CE, describe three doshas (vāta, pitta and kapha) whose balance is held to produce health, and they also describe surgical techniques such as cataract surgery and rhinoplasty. The theory and practice of Ayurveda are considered pseudoscientific. Many preparations, particularly in the rasashastra tradition, contain toxic levels of lead, mercury and [[Arsenic]]. There is no evidence that cancer can be treated or cured through Ayurveda.

Siamese kingdom in [[Southeast Asia]] (1351–1767), centered on the city of Ayutthaya. Considered the precursor of modern [[Thailand]], it emerged from a group of maritime city-states in the lower Chao Phraya valley. Its name derives from the [[Sanskrit]] Ayodhya. From 1569 to 1584 it was a vassal of Toungoo Burma under [[Bayinnaung]], then regained independence. In the 17th and 18th centuries it became a center of international trade. Under Narai (r. 1657–1688) Persian and then European influence was strong, and an embassy went to the court of [[Louis XIV]] in 1686. Cultural life centered on [[Theravada]] Buddhism. In 1767, after a 14-month siege, Burmese forces destroyed the city, ending the 417-year-old kingdom. Within fifteen years the seat of authority had moved to Thonburi and [[Bangkok]].

Flowering shrub in the genus [[Rhododendron]] and family [[Ericaceae]]. Azaleas bloom in spring, often for several weeks, and tolerate shade. They do best in well-drained acidic soil at 4.5–6.0 pH and need little fertilizer. Breeders have produced thousands of cultivars, which are propagated by cuttings. *Azalea indica* was first introduced to the outdoor landscape in the United States in the 1830s, at a rice plantation near [[Charleston, South Carolina]]. The plant is highly toxic, and in Turkey bees fed on its nectar produce an occasionally lethal honey known as mad honey. The azalea is one of the symbols of [[São Paulo]], and in China it is known as "thinking of home bush", immortalized in the poetry of [[Du Fu]].

Landlocked country in the South Caucasus, at the boundary of Western Asia and Eastern Europe. Its capital and largest city is [[Baku]], on the [[Caspian Sea]]. The territory was ruled first by Caucasian Albania and later by Persian empires, until the Russian Empire took the region in the 19th century. The Azerbaijan Democratic Republic declared independence in 1918 and became the first secular democratic Muslim-majority state. In 1920 the country was incorporated into the [[Soviet Union]] as the Azerbaijan SSR. It proclaimed independence on August 30, 1991, shortly before the Soviet Union dissolved. In 2023 an Azerbaijani offensive ended the self-proclaimed Republic of Artsakh in [[Nagorno-Karabakh]], and most of its ethnic Armenian residents left. About 97% of the population is Muslim, and the constitution declares no official religion. The ruling New Azerbaijan Party has been in power since 1993, and critics have accused the Aliyev family of authoritarianism, citing media restrictions and repression of the [[Shia Islam|Shia Muslim]] population. Oil and natural gas account for roughly two-thirds of GDP.

Turkic language of the Oghuz branch, also known as Azeri. It is the only official language of the [[Azerbaijan|Republic of Azerbaijan]] and one of 14 official languages of [[Dagestan]], a Russian federal subject. It lacks official status in Iran, where most Iranian Azerbaijanis live. North Azerbaijani, based on the Shirvani dialect, has used the [[Latin script]] since independence in 1991, while South Azerbaijani has always used the Perso-Arabic script. The two varieties are highly mutually intelligible but differ in phonology, lexicon, morphology and syntax, and the International Organization for Standardization treats them as distinct languages. The language evolved from Oghuz Turkic under strong Persian influence and is closely related to Turkmen and Turkish.

[[Antibiotic]] of the azalide subclass of macrolides, sold as Zithromax. It treats bacterial infections including middle ear infections, strep throat, [[Pneumonia|pneumonia]], traveler's diarrhea and sexually transmitted infections. It binds the bacterial [[Ribosome|ribosome]], inhibiting protein production. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting and diarrhea, and it can prolong the QT interval, which may cause life-threatening arrhythmias. Discovered in [[Croatia]] in 1980 by the pharmaceutical company Pliva, it was approved for medical use in 1988 and is on the [[World Health Organization]]'s List of Essential Medicines. In 2023 it was the 64th most commonly prescribed medication in the United States, with more than 10 million prescriptions.

Portuguese archipelago of nine volcanic islands in the [[Atlantic Ocean]]. The Azores are one of Portugal's two autonomous regions, with [[Madeira]], and a special territory of the [[European Union]]. The islands lie in three groups and extend for more than 600 km. Mount Pico on Pico island is the highest point in Portugal, at 2,351 m. The islands sit at a triple junction where the North American, Eurasian and Nubian plates meet. The climate is mild, influenced by the [[Gulf Stream]], and the economy relies on agriculture, dairy farming, fishing and tourism. Portuguese settlement began in the 15th century, sponsored by [[Prince Henry the Navigator]]. The largest city is Ponta Delgada.

Alliance of three Nahua city-states in central Mexico (1428–1521). Also called the Triple Alliance, it was formed from the victorious factions of a civil war against Azcapotzalco, and [[Tenochtitlan]] became militarily dominant. Its rule was hegemonic: conquered cities kept their rulers if they paid semi-annual tribute and supplied troops. At its height the alliance controlled most of central Mexico, as well as the distant Xoconochco province near the present-day Guatemalan border. In 1521 Spanish conquistadors under [[Hernán Cortés]] and their native allies defeated the empire.

Polytheistic and monistic pantheism of the [[Aztec Empire]]. Nahua metaphysics centered on teotl, a sacred power construed as the supreme god Ometeotl. Priests and the upper classes held monistic views, while popular religion emphasized the mythological and polytheistic aspects of a pantheon of lesser gods and natural forces. The most important deities, including Huitzilopochtli, were worshiped at the Templo Mayor in [[Tenochtitlan]], and conquered peoples could add the imperial god to their own pantheons. The cosmology divided the world into thirteen heavens and nine earthly layers. The Sun, the Moon and the planet [[Venus]] were the most important celestial entities. Public ritual included food, dance, ceremonial warfare and [[Human sacrifice|human sacrifice]]. After the Spanish conquest the population was obliged to convert to Catholicism, and the two religions syncretized, as seen in the [[Day of the Dead]].

British public service broadcaster headquartered at Broadcasting House in [[London]]. Founded as the British Broadcasting Company on October 18, 1922, it became a public corporation under royal charter on January 1, 1927. It is funded mainly by an annual television license fee set by the government and agreed by Parliament. Since April 1, 2014, it has also funded the BBC World Service, which broadcasts in 43 languages. Its commercial subsidiary, BBC Studios, sells programs internationally. In 1923 it launched *Radio Times*, the first broadcast listings magazine. The BBC has faced criticism over its impartiality, funding and coverage of the [[Iraq War]], and accusations of political bias have come from both the left and the right.

Erotic practices and roleplay involving [[Bondage (BDSM)|bondage]], discipline, [[Dominance and submission|dominance and submission]], and [[Sadomasochism|sadomasochism]]. The initialism, first recorded in a [[Usenet]] post in 1991, combines B/D (bondage and discipline), D/s (dominance and submission) and S/M (sadism and masochism). Participants usually take complementary roles involving unequal power, so the informed consent of all partners is considered essential. The dominant partner, or dom, takes psychological control over the submissive, or sub. People who change between roles are called switches. Activities are often confined to an agreed period called a scene. Inclusion in the community often depends on self-identification and shared experience. Some research reports that participants show average or above-average psychological health.

German manufacturer of luxury vehicles and motorcycles, headquartered in [[Munich]]. The company began as an aircraft engine producer, moved into motorcycles after World War I and later entered the automobile market. Its vehicles are sold under the BMW, Mini and Rolls-Royce brands, and its motorcycles under BMW Motorrad. In 2023 it produced 2,555,341 vehicles, the world's ninth-largest total for motor vehicles. Investments by the Quandt family in 1959 saved the company from [[Bankruptcy|bankruptcy]], and the family remains a long-term shareholder.

British multinational oil and gas company headquartered in [[London]]. One of the oil and gas supermajors, it is vertically integrated across exploration, refining, distribution and trading. It originated as the Anglo-Persian Oil Company, founded in 1909 to exploit oil discovered in [[Iran]], and adopted the name British Petroleum in 1954. The British government privatized the company in stages from 1979 to 1987. Its worst environmental catastrophe was the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill in the [[Gulf of Mexico]], which leaked about 4.9 million barrels. The company's fines and penalties for the spill cost more than $4.5 billion.

Intergovernmental organization of ten countries, founded by Brazil, Russia, India and China. The term BRIC was coined by British economist Jim O'Neill in 2001 and later championed by [[Goldman Sachs]]. The group held its first summit in 2009, and South Africa joined in 2010. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates joined in 2024, and Indonesia in early 2025. Together the members comprise more than a quarter of the global economy and nearly half the world's population. The New Development Bank, based in [[Shanghai]], finances infrastructure projects. Some commentators see BRICS as an alternative to the [[G7]], while others describe it as an incoherent affiliation.

South Korean boy band, also known as the Bangtan Boys. The group debuted in 2013 under Big Hit Entertainment with the single album *2 Cool 4 Skool*. It became the first act from South Korea to top the Billboard 200, with *Love Yourself: Tear* (2018), and the first all-South Korean act to reach number one on the Billboard Hot 100 with "Dynamite". As of 2023 it was the best-selling musical act in South Korean history, with more than 40 million albums sold. The group partnered with [[UNICEF]] in 2017 on the Love Myself anti-violence campaign. Its members completed mandatory military service by June 2025.

Chinese automotive subsidiary of BYD Company, headquartered in [[Shenzhen]]. Established in January 2003 after BYD acquired the struggling Xi'an Qinchuan Automobile, it produces battery electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, known in China as new energy vehicles, along with electric buses and trucks. Its parent supplies batteries, motors and electronic controls, and its battery subsidiary makes [[Lithium|lithium]] iron phosphate batteries, including the Blade battery. BYD became China's best-selling car brand in 2023, overtaking [[Volkswagen]]. In 2025 it overtook Tesla to become the world's largest electric carmaker. The company has faced scrutiny over aggressive price cuts, labor issues and environmental concerns.

American [[Blues|blues]] guitarist, singer and songwriter, known as the King of the Blues. Born on a cotton plantation in Mississippi and raised in the Mississippi Delta, he taught himself guitar and began his career on local radio. Working at WDIA in [[Memphis, Tennessee|Memphis]], he was nicknamed Blues Boy, later shortened to B. B. He introduced a style of soloing based on fluid string bending and vibrato that influenced many later [[Electric guitar|electric guitar]] players. He was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 1987. His 1969 hit "The Thrill Is Gone" won a [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]]. In 1956 alone he appeared at 342 shows, and he performed more than 200 concerts a year into his 70s.
